PINK1 is a mitochondrial kinase that, upon mitochondrial damage, accumulates on the outer mitochondrial membrane, is auto-phosphorylated, and phosphorylates ubiquitin and parkin at conserved residue Ser65; parkin is a cytosolic E3 ubiquitin ligase; together they mediate mitochondrial quality control and mitophagy

PINK1 dimerizes into a supermolecular protein complex; PINK1/parkin pathway amplifies phosphorylated poly-ubiquitin chains; p.G411S mutant interferes with wild-type PINK1 function through dimerization in heterozygotes (heterodimeric complex)
Under physiological conditions PINK1 protein is imported into the inner mitochondrial membrane; mitochondrial damage directs PINK1 to the outer mitochondrial membrane
Levels of phosphorylated p-Ser65-Ub are disease-relevant, mitochondrial stress-specific markers and reporters for PINK1 and parkin enzymatic activities

Patient fibroblasts and induced neurons from p.G411S heterozygotes showed sustained significant reduction in kinase activity without protein decrease; p.Q456X heterozygotes showed reduced PINK1 protein and decreased initial kinase activity
